subject: language_arts

unit.title: Word classes & sentence types
unit.essentialQuestion: What jobs do words do, and how do sentences come in different types?

title: Joining clauses: and / but / or, and because / when / if / that
objectives: By the end, I can join two ideas with the right conjunction, including because for a reason.

vocabulary.definition: a joining word that glues two ideas together
vocabulary.example: and, but, or, because, when, if

vocabulary.definition: join equal ideas: and adds, but shows a difference, or gives a choice
vocabulary.example: I like cats and dogs. It's small but strong.

vocabulary.definition: the reason word — it must be followed by a real reason
vocabulary.example: I wore my coat because it was cold.

vocabulary.definition: when adds a time; if adds a maybe
vocabulary.example: We'll play outside when it stops raining. If it snows, we'll build a snowman.

emphasize: The joining word must MATCH THE MEANING: and adds, but contrasts, or chooses, because gives a reason, when a time, if a maybe.
because must be followed by a REAL reason — and the reason comes AFTER because ('I went to bed because I was tired', not 'I was tired because I went to bed').
Pre-empt joining everything with 'and' — stop and ask: add? difference? choice? reason?

keyConcepts: subordination: because/when/if/that add an extra part
because = reason; the reason follows because
misconceptions: because with no real reason after it, or the clauses in the wrong order (the reason must follow because)
using 'but' where a reason is needed (contrast vs cause)
hooks: 'I was happy.' …Why, though? Add the magic word BECAUSE and tell us: 'I was happy because it was my birthday!'
priorKnowledge: what a sentence is; end marks (Lessons 18–19)

digital: conjunction bank with meanings on screen

plan.goal: Feel the power of because: a bare statement begs for a reason; retrieve two tiny sentences to join later.
plan.note: Let the child invent the birthday-style reason — their reason, their sentence.
plan.successCriteria: Child completes 'I was happy because…' with a real reason and offers two tiny sentences about a dog.

script.say: I was happy. …Why, though? That sentence is hiding the best part! Add the magic word BECAUSE and tell us the reason: I was happy because it was my birthday! Today we join ideas with exactly the right word. Your turn — finish it your way: I was happy because… And while you're warm: give me two tiny sentences about a dog. We'll join them later!
script.adaptHints: Accept any genuine reason with delight. Keep the child's two dog sentences to reuse in the example beat.

stuckProtocol: If no reason comes: offer two choices aloud — 'because it was sunny, or because you had cake?' — then let the child pick or invent a third.

plan.goal: Meet the two conjunction families: and/but/or join equal ideas; because/when/if/that add an extra part. Underline because + reason.
plan.note: The meanings table is the anchor. Say each conjunction's one-word meaning every time: adds, difference, choice, reason, time, maybe.
plan.successCriteria: Child can say what each of and/but/or/because does, and that because tells us WHY.

script.say: Conjunctions join ideas. Some join EQUAL ideas: and — it adds: I like cats and dogs. But — it shows a difference: It's small but strong. Or — a choice: apple or pear? Others add an extra part: because — a reason. When — a time. If — a maybe. That — it points. Watch: I wore my coat because it was cold. The word because tells us WHY — and listen: the reason comes straight after it. Pick the joining word that matches the meaning — because equals a reason.
script.adaptHints: Tap the table row as each conjunction is named. Underline 'because it was cold' with a flourish — 'there's the reason, right after because.'

rows: I wore my coat because it was cold.
We play outside when it is sunny.
If it snows, we'll build a snowman.

plan.goal: Shared joining: pick the reason word for 'It was raining' + 'we stayed in'; then join with or; quick meaning check.
plan.note: Ask the meaning question every time: add? difference? choice? reason? The child's own dog sentences from the hook get joined here too.
plan.successCriteria: Child chooses because for the rain pair, or for the fruit pair, and answers 'because' to the reason question.

script.say: Join these two with me: It was raining — we stayed in. Which word shows WHY we stayed in? Ask yourself: are we adding? Showing a difference? Choosing? Or giving a reason? … Now this one: You can have an apple — a pear. Adding, or choosing? … And those two dog sentences you gave me earlier — let's join them with the word that fits!
script.adaptHints: Reuse the child's own hook sentences verbatim. If they pick 'so' for the rain pair, honour it — 'so works too! Today our reason word is because: we stayed in because it was raining.'

blocks.prompt: It was raining ___ we stayed in. Which joining word shows WHY?
options: so we can say: We stayed in because it was raining
blocks.explain: The rain is the REASON we stayed in — the reason word is because: We stayed in because it was raining.

check.question: Which word shows a reason: and, but, because?

wrongAnswers.why: defaulting to the all-purpose joiner
wrongAnswers.remedy: 'And' just adds more. Which of the three tells you WHY something happened?

wrongAnswers.why: contrast confused with cause
wrongAnswers.remedy: 'But' shows a difference — two ideas pulling apart. Which word glues an idea to its REASON?

plan.goal: Key diagnostic: 'I was tired ___ I went to bed.' — because beats and/but; probe what because tells the reader.
plan.note: 'and' is the defaulting trap; 'but' is the contrast-for-cause trap. Probe after success: 'what does because tell the reader?'
plan.successCriteria: Child picks because and says it tells the reader the reason (why).

script.say: Finish with the BEST word: I was tired ___ I went to bed. Your choices: and, but, because. Think about the meaning — is the second idea an add-on, a difference, or the reason?
script.adaptHints: After a correct answer, probe: 'What does because tell the reader?' (the reason). Then flip it playfully: 'I went to bed because I was tired — same reason, spot it after because!'

blocks.prompt: I was tired ___ I went to bed.
blocks.explain: Being tired is the reason for going to bed — because glues the idea to its reason. (Best of all: I went to bed because I was tired.)

check.question: Finish with the best word: 'I was tired ___ I went to bed.' (and / but / because)
check.expectedAnswer: because — it tells the reader the reason

wrongAnswers.why: defaulting to and
wrongAnswers.remedy: Does 'and' tell us WHY? We need the reason word — which one is it?

wrongAnswers.why: picked a contrast for a reason
wrongAnswers.remedy: 'But' shows a difference. Going to bed BECAUSE you're tired is a reason — which word gives reasons?

plan.goal: Independent joining: five sentences with the meaning-matched conjunction (mix of and/but/or/because); interleave when/if once secure.
plan.note: Director draws from practiceBank, start level 2. Watch for: over-using and; because with no real reason after it; clause order slips with because/when/if.
plan.successCriteria: Child completes five joins choosing by meaning, including a reasoned because.

script.say: Your glue gun now! Five sentences are coming, each with a gap. Before you pick a word, ask the four questions: adding? difference? choice? reason? The bank with meanings is right there if you need it.
script.adaptHints: Frame the sentence content around the child's interests (football, pets, space) — the meanings never change. Once secure, slip in a when/if item.

stuckProtocol: Name why: 'The meaning and the joining word don't match yet.'
Read the two ideas aloud and ask: add? difference? choice? reason?
ONE hint: point to the conjunction bank meanings.
Re-ask an easy and/because pair, then build back.
Keep it safe: 'Mistakes show us what to practise — smaller step.'

plan.goal: Child produces a because sentence with a genuine reason; end on a win with process praise.
plan.note: Child-led. The genuine reason IS the mastery evidence — listen for it.
plan.successCriteria: Child says a full sentence: idea + because + a real reason.

script.say: Last one, all yours: tell me a sentence with because and a REAL reason. … Beautiful. You stopped reaching for 'and' and chose the word that fit the meaning — that's precise writing.
script.adaptHints: If the reason is thin ('because yes'), smile and ask 'because WHAT happened?' — then celebrate the upgraded version.

wrongAnswers.why: contrast word where nothing contrasts
wrongAnswers.remedy: 'But' pulls two ideas apart — do cats and dogs disagree here? You like BOTH. Which word adds one to the other?

wrongAnswers.why: reason word with no reason present
wrongAnswers.remedy: Is 'dogs' the REASON you like cats? No — it's just one more thing you like. Which word simply adds?

hints: Which word ADDS one more thing?

reteach.say: 'And' is the adding word — it stacks likes together like blocks: I like cats AND dogs AND rabbits. No difference, no choice, no reason — just adding. That's and's whole job.

practiceBank.skill: recognise because as the reason word

block.prompt: Which joining word shows a REASON?
block.explain: because glues an idea to its reason — it answers 'why?'

wrongAnswers.why: defaulting to the familiar joiner
wrongAnswers.remedy: 'And' just adds more. If I ask you WHY, which word starts your answer?

wrongAnswers.why: contrast confused with cause
wrongAnswers.remedy: 'But' shows a difference. Try answering 'Why are you smiling?' — do you start with but, or because?

hints: I was happy ___ it was my birthday.

reteach.say: Whenever anyone asks WHY, one word rushes to help: because! Why did you wear a coat? Because it was cold. Why were you happy? Because it was my birthday. Because is the reason word — that's its only job, and it does it brilliantly.

block.definition: the reason word — it answers 'why?' and the reason comes right after it

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: but (The spider is small but strong.)

wrongAnswers.why: defaulting to and — missing the surprise
wrongAnswers.remedy: Small AND strong just stacks them — but there's a surprise here! Small things usually aren't strong. Which word shows that difference?

wrongAnswers.why: choice word where nothing is being chosen
wrongAnswers.remedy: Is the spider choosing between small and strong? It's BOTH — and that's surprising. Which word shows a difference?

hints: Small… yet strong — that's a surprise!
Which word shows two ideas pulling different ways?

reteach.say: 'But' is the surprise word — it joins two ideas that pull against each other. Small BUT strong. Tired BUT happy. When the second idea makes you go 'ooh, really?', that's but's moment.

block.caption: small BUT strong — ideas pulling different ways

block.text: You can have an apple ___ a pear.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: or (You can have an apple or a pear.)

wrongAnswers.why: adding when the sentence offers a pick-one choice
wrongAnswers.remedy: With 'and' you'd get BOTH! This sentence offers a pick. Which word says 'choose one'?

wrongAnswers.why: reason word with no reason
wrongAnswers.remedy: Is the pear the REASON for the apple? No — they're two choices on a plate. Which word offers a choice?

reteach.say: 'Or' is the choosing word — it holds up two things and says: pick one! An apple OR a pear. Football OR tag. When only one can happen, or does the joining.

block.caption: or = choose one: an apple OR a pear

practiceBank.skill: complete a because sentence with a real reason

block.prompt: Finish this with a REAL reason: 'I was late because…' — make it true-sounding (or wonderfully silly, as long as it's a reason!)
block.sample: I was late because a duck stole my shoe.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: Any completion that is a genuine reason, e.g. 'because I missed the bus' / 'because a duck stole my shoe'

wrongAnswers.answer: I was late because I was late.
wrongAnswers.why: circular — repeats the idea instead of giving a reason
wrongAnswers.remedy: That tells me you were late twice! WHAT happened to make you late? The bit after because must be the why.

wrongAnswers.answer: I was late because and then I ran.
wrongAnswers.why: conjunction pile-up — no clear reason clause
wrongAnswers.remedy: One glue word at a time! After because, give me just the reason: 'because I…' what?

hints: Ask yourself: what MADE you late?

reteach.say: The bit after because has one job: to be the reason. Test it with the why-question: Why were you late? …because a duck stole my shoe! If your ending answers the why, because is happy. If it doesn't — no glue!

block.title: Because test
steps: Say the idea: I was late
The answer goes after because: …because I missed the bus.

block.prompt: Match each joining word to its job.

wrongAnswers.why: contrast and cause muddled
wrongAnswers.remedy: Try it in a sentence: 'I went to bed but I was tired'? Strange! Which word makes that sentence make sense — and what does but really show?

wrongAnswers.why: or treated like and
wrongAnswers.remedy: 'An apple or a pear' — do you get both? No, you pick! What does or offer?

hints: Say each one in a sentence to test it.

reteach.say: Four glue words, four jobs, no overlaps: and stacks, but surprises, or offers, because explains. Keep the four questions handy — adding? difference? choice? reason? — and the right glue picks itself.

block.text: We will go to the park ___ it stops raining.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: when (We will go to the park when it stops raining.)

wrongAnswers.why: contrast word forced into a time slot
wrongAnswers.remedy: Is the rain stopping a SURPRISE against the park? No — it's the TIME you'll go. Which word adds a time?

wrongAnswers.why: choice word where there's no choice
wrongAnswers.remedy: Park or rain-stopping — are we picking one? No! The second part tells us WHEN. Which word does time?

hints: The second part tells you the TIME it will happen.
when = a time; if = a maybe.

reteach.say: when and if are cousins: when adds a TIME that will come — we'll go WHEN it stops raining. if adds a MAYBE — we'll build a snowman IF it snows (it might not!). Time you can wait for: when. Maybe: if.

block.prompt: Detective work! Which sentence uses because correctly?
options: I put on my coat because it was cold.
It was cold because I put on my coat.
I put on my coat because.
block.explain: The reason must follow because: the cold is WHY the coat went on. Sentence 2 says your coat made the weather cold — magic coat! Sentence 3 gives no reason at all.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: I put on my coat because it was cold.

wrongAnswers.answer: It was cold because I put on my coat.
wrongAnswers.why: clauses swapped — the reason and the result traded places
wrongAnswers.remedy: Read it slowly — did your coat MAKE the weather cold? Which thing caused which? Put the real reason after because.

wrongAnswers.answer: I put on my coat because.
wrongAnswers.why: because left hanging with no reason clause
wrongAnswers.remedy: Because made a promise — a reason is coming! — and then nothing came. Finish it: because WHAT?

hints: Ask: which part is the REASON? It goes after because.
Could a coat make the weather cold?

reteach.say: Because points backwards at the why. The cold came first — THAT's the reason — so it sits after because: I put on my coat because it was cold. Swap them and your coat controls the weather! Always ask: which part caused which?

rows: I put on my coat because it was cold.
It was cold because I put on my coat.
I put on my coat because.

block.prompt: Sentence builder! Put the words in order — remember, the reason follows because.

practiceBank.expectedAnswer: I wore my coat because it was cold.

wrongAnswers.answer: It was cold because I wore my coat (reversed clauses)
wrongAnswers.why: reason and result swapped around because
wrongAnswers.remedy: Check with the why-question: why did you wear the coat? The answer — it was cold — goes AFTER because.

wrongAnswers.answer: Because it was cold I wore my coat (no comma awareness)
wrongAnswers.why: starting with because — fine in Y3+, but today's pattern is idea + because + reason
wrongAnswers.remedy: You CAN start with because — clever! — but today build it our way: say what you did first, then because, then the why.

hints: because sits in the middle; the reason comes after it.

reteach.say: Build it in three chunks, like train carriages: the doing — I wore my coat. The glue — because. The why — it was cold. Hook them up: I wore my coat because it was cold. Doing, glue, why — in that order, every time today.

block.title: Three carriages
steps: 🚂 the doing: I wore my coat

adaptivity.levelUp: 2 consecutive correct at the current level → next level; at level 3, interleave and/but/or, because, and when/if items.
adaptivity.levelDown: 2 misses on the same skill → run the item's reteach with the conjunction bank meanings on screen, then a level-1 item (and vs because only).
adaptivity.masterySignal: 3+ correct across levels 2–3 including one because item with a genuine reason in the right order and one but-or-or contrast/choice item → mastery ≥ 0.8 for 'conjunctions'.
struggleProtocol: Name why: 'The meaning and the joining word don't match yet.'
Read the two ideas aloud and ask: add? difference? choice? reason?
ONE hint: point to the conjunction bank meanings.
Re-ask an easy and/because pair, then build back.
Keep it safe: 'Mistakes show us what to practise — smaller step.'
adaptivity.personalization: Build sentence content from the learner's world (matches, pets, playdates) — 'I was excited because…' invites their true reasons. The four meaning-questions never change.
adaptivity.endOnSuccess: Finish on a winnable join; praise the process — 'you stopped reaching for and and matched the word to the meaning.'

differentiation.support: Conjunction bank with child-friendly meanings stays beside every item; start with and-vs-because pairs only.
differentiation.stretch: Write a sentence using when or if correctly, then one with that ('I think that…'); explain why 'It was cold because I put on my coat' is backwards.

extension: Finish three silly 'I was late because…' sentences with your own reasons — the sillier the better, as long as each one is truly a reason.
assessmentEvidence: Child joins clauses with the meaning-correct conjunction across five sentences and gives a real reason after because (in the right clause order).
revisitLater: because-reasons power the inference work in Unit 5 ('because the text says…'). Re-pose one join as retrieval next session; when/if return in Year 3 subordination.
